chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated that from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about madhy, and he instructed me to perform wudu (ablution) because of it. Then I repeated the question to him another year, and he instructed me to perform wudu (ablution) because of it. And he said: Indeed, 'Ali عليه السلام instructed al-Miqdad to ask the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, but he felt shy to ask him, so he said: concerning it, there is wudu (ablution). I said: And if I do not perform wudu (ablution)? He said: There is no harm.

So this report came clarified and explained, indicating that the command to perform wudu (ablution) because of it was only for a kind of recommendation, not obligation. And it is possible that the recommendation in repeating wudu (ablution) due to madhy is directed only toward one from whom madhy exits with desire; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: Recommendation, showing the ruling is preferable rather than binding.
key_terms.الْإِيجَابِ: Obligation, negated here to show the act is not mandatory.
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: Pre-seminal fluid discussed here as the subject of ritual purity ruling.
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: Wudu (ablution), mentioned here as the act commanded in relation to madhy.
key_terms.بِشَهْوَةٍ: With desire, indicating a contextual condition mentioned in the explanatory note.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: An expression indicating there is no problem or harm in leaving it.

ai.seo_question: Does madhy make wudu obligatory in Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of madhy and indicates that performing wudu (ablution) after it is recommended rather than obligatory. It also connects the ruling to a report involving Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, al-Miqdad, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, showing its basis in prophetic tradition.
